<reason>A wins by distinguishing broad open licensing from enforceable access and research reuse, then making its alternative concrete under pressure. B retained a genuine advantage on frictionless downstream reuse, but its closing still portrayed immediately exercisable permissions as dependence on future generosity. A also exposed the gap between recognizing community exceptions and identifying the interests they protect before release. These rebuttals left A with the cleaner comparison between reduced reuse friction and difficult-to-reverse licensing mistakes.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A answered the post-grant-access challenge with institutional deposits, immediate research-reuse permissions, and enforceable release schedules. B’s subsequent “promise versus present right” framing did not adequately engage that answer, weakening its central claim that rejecting the open-license default necessarily leaves researchers waiting.</best_rebuttal>
